chat.ts.unchanged: sendChat(deps, text), ollamaChat(gf, settings, history), cloudChat(gf, settings, key, history, origin), probeLocalModel, buildHistory keep their behaviour and call shape (extra trailing options are optional).
chat.ts.ChatService: new ChatService(deps: ChatDeps). start(text, {onDelta?}) returns {id, cancel(), done: Promise<ChatMessage>}; cancel(id?) returns boolean; busy getter. One generation at a time (a second start rejects 'already being generated'). Wire to IPC as chat:start (push deltas to the renderer from onDelta, return id) and chat:cancel.
chat.ts.cancel_behaviour: Partial text is stored as an assistant message (source local|cloud) followed by a system note 'Stopped by you...'. The note says whether the cloud provider may have the message. System notes are never sent back to a model.
chat.ts.ChatDeps.profile: optional () => {keepAlive, numCtx} | undefined; applies to local chats only. Pass ModelRuntime.chatProfile.
chat.ts.resolveChatRoute(settings, keyConfigured: pure; online without key is denied and never becomes a local request.
chat.ts.helpers: readLines, readNdjson, readSseData, withIdleSignal (120 s idle timeout for streams), ChatCancelled, STREAM_IDLE_MS

models.ts.ModelRuntime: new ModelRuntime({fetch: guardedFetch, settings, ramGB?, guard?, io?, adapters?, newId, now?, onJob?, onProfile?, initialProfile?}). Methods: version(), list(), running(), health(), select(name,{warm?,unloadOthers?}) -> settings patch only (does NOT save settings), unload(name?), profile(), setProfile(id), chatProfile, capabilities(), downloadsStatus(), overview(), validatePack(dir), startImport(dir,name?), startPull(model), jobs(), cancelJob(id).
models.ts.ModelsClient: Type for the renderer-facing IPC bridge; methods map 1:1 to ModelRuntime (overview, select, unload, setProfile, validatePack, startImport, startPull, cancelJob, optional pickPackFolder).
models.ts.ModelActionGuard: async ({kind:'pull'|'import', model, endpoint, detail}) => {allowed, reason?}. Must be supplied by native main as a trusted dialog.showMessageBox callback (Cancel default). Never a renderer boolean. Without it downloads are refused; import runs without it but may use it.
models.ts.resource_profiles: default (legacy: Ollama default context, 2m keep_alive), low-memory, balanced, performance; recommendProfile(ramGB, modelBytes).
models.ts.model_pack: Folder with modelpack.json {format:'desktop-companion-modelpack', version:1, name, files:[{path,sha256,bytes}], template?, system?, parameters?}. Only .gguf, plain relative paths, no symlinks; sizes and SHA-256 verified before any upload. Import = HEAD/POST /api/blobs then POST /api/create with files digests, all via the loopback 'ollama' purpose.
models.ts.adapter_contracts: VisionAdapter, EmbeddingAdapter, FineTuneAdapter, ModelAdapters (types only; no implementation).

interfaces.Models.tsx: <Models client={ModelsClient|null} currentModel onUseModel={(patch)=>Promise<void>} /> plus presentational ModelsView (props only, used by tests). Uses existing primitives and CSS classes (page, two-col, stack, cap-list, cap-row, row, field-hint, input, mono); the 'row' class and the native <progress> element have no dedicated styling from this module. Shows a browser-preview state when client is null.

dependencies.runtime: No new npm dependencies. Uses node:fs, node:crypto, global fetch/ReadableStream/TransformStream/AbortSignal.any (Node 20+, Electron 44).
needs_from_captain: IPC handlers in main/preload for ModelsClient and chat start/cancel/delta (shared contracts and backend are not owned by this module).
A trusted guard callback for ModelRuntime (dialog.showMessageBox, Cancel default) and a pickPackFolder bridge using the native folder picker.
Saving the settings patch returned by ModelRuntime.select through the existing saveSettings path (AI connection change confirmation applies).
Navigation entry and a Settings/ModelRuntime profile persistence hook (onProfile) if the profile should survive restart; Settings has no profile field so it is in memory only.
Optionally route system.ts local-llm probing and speech capabilities through ModelRuntime/Speech.status for consistent reasons.

limitations: Offline pack import, pull, unload and switch are verified only against fake Ollama servers. They were not run against a real Ollama; the /api/blobs + /api/create 'files' flow depends on the installed Ollama version and a 404 from create is reported as unsupported. No minimum version is enforced.

Model download is performed by the local Ollama process, not by this app; the network guard only sees loopback traffic. The offline/online and guard checks live in ModelRuntime.startPull and must stay wired to a trusted native dialog.
Importing a pack reads each file twice (hash, then upload), and a file changed between the two steps is rejected by Ollama's own digest check rather than by this module.
Resource profile is held in memory (no Settings field, shared contracts not editable here) and resets to 'default' on restart unless the captain persists it.

Streaming chat is implemented and tested in the service, but the current backend still calls the non-streaming sendChat; the UI gets no tokens or Stop button until the captain wires ChatService over IPC.

Cancelling a local generation closes the HTTP request; Ollama stops generating on disconnect, but this was not confirmed against a real server. Cancelling a native transcription only discards the result: the PowerShell helper runs until its own timeout.

Local vision, embeddings and fine-tuning are reported unsupported. The model's reported capabilities are shown, but there is no image, embedding or training pipeline; adapters are type contracts only.
Speech remains Windows System.Speech only (basic dictation quality). No neural TTS or Whisper engine is bundled; the engine adapter contracts are exercised only with test doubles.
Microphone helpers (permission, device list, recorder) are untested against real hardware by design; only their pure logic and degraded paths are covered.
defaults stay generic: localModel remains llama3.2:3b in validation.ts (not owned here). The recorded qwen3.5:2b setup is documented in docs only and was not re-run.

Models.tsx was verified by static markup tests and a successful vite build, not in a live window or with a screen reader; no CSS was added, so progress bars and the 'row' layout use whatever styles the shell provides.
